question: Two similar bus joints under similar load differ by 18 °C. Table 100.18 says:
choices: Possible deficiency; investigate when convenient next year
Major discrepancy; repair immediately
Normal, because ambient was not recorded
The table does not use Celsius
explanation: Above 15 °C between similar components is the 'repair immediately' row. 1–3 °C is investigate, 4–15 °C is repair as time permits. The table is written in °C. Load still matters, and this is not permission to open the gear without a shock and arc-flash plan.

question: Two similar lugs under similar load differ by 8 °C. Table 100.18 calls that:
choices: Possible deficiency; investigate
Probable deficiency; repair as time permits
Major discrepancy; repair immediately
Normal, because it is under 15 °C
explanation: 4 °C to 15 °C between similar components is the probable-deficiency row: repair as time permits. 1–3 °C is only “investigate.” Above 15 °C is immediate. 8 °C is in the middle band.

question: A connection is 45 °C hotter than the surrounding air, with no similar part to compare. Table 100.18 says:
choices: Monitor it
Repair immediately
Ignore air comparisons
Possible deficiency only
explanation: Above 40 °C over ambient is the major-discrepancy row. The 21–40 °C ambient band is the one that says monitor until you can fix it. Similar-part ΔT and ambient ΔT are different columns.

question: A part runs 30 °C above ambient and you have no similar component. Table 100.18 says:
choices: Repair immediately
Monitor until corrective measures can be done
Possible deficiency only
The table does not use ambient
explanation: 21 °C to 40 °C above ambient is the monitor row. Above 40 °C above ambient, or above 15 °C between similar parts, is immediate. 30 °C over air is not yet that immediate row.

question: NFPA 70B-2026 infrared inspections are made:
choices: On de-energized gear with all covers sealed
Online, under operating load, with only the necessary accessible covers removed
At no load, so the camera is safer
Once, with no delta-T written down
explanation: Compare similar parts under similar load, or compare with ambient. Record the temperature difference and what it was compared to. A cover that does not have to come off stays on. These chapters do not give a degrees-of-rise limit, so the bank does not invent one.

question: In NFPA 70B-2026 Table 9.3.2, infrared thermography for conditions 1, 2, and 3 is:
choices: 60, 36, and 12 months, the row labeled standard
12, 12, and 6 months
36, 24, and 12 months
Before each use
explanation: Thermography stays on 12, 12, and 6 months. The plain standard row, used for many assemblies when the manufacturer is silent, is 60, 36, and 12 months. Do not put the infrared camera on that longer row.

question: You scan a clean, shiny copper bus joint and a painted steel bracket that are at the same real temperature. Which reading is more likely to mislead you?
choices: The bracket, because paint color raises emissivity
Neither, because imagers correct for material automatically
The copper; shiny metal has low emissivity
The bracket, because steel conducts heat poorly
explanation: Shiny metals emit poorly and reflect a lot, so the camera sees part of the surroundings. Painted or oxidized surfaces are usually around 0.7 to 0.9. The camera cannot tell emitted energy from reflected energy on its own. Source: IEEE C57.152-2025, Annex C.2.

question: Two painted covers have the same finish texture, one black and one white. For infrared emissivity:
choices: Color matters little; finish and condition do
Black always has much higher emissivity than white
White has higher emissivity because it reflects light
Only the darker cover can be scanned
explanation: Visible color does not set infrared emissivity. Surface condition (gloss, oxidation, dirt) does. Two covers with the same paint finish behave about the same. Source: IEEE C57.152-2025, Annex C.2.

question: Outdoors on a sunny day, a hot spot shows up on a shiny connector. A quick way to tell a reflection from real heating is to:
choices: Raise the emissivity setting to 1.0
Zoom in until the spot fills the screen
Wait for the reading to stabilize
View it from another angle
explanation: Changing the viewing angle (C57.152 suggests moving about 90 degrees) moves a reflection but not a real hot spot. Solar heating of the surface is a separate effect from solar reflection. Source: IEEE C57.152-2025, Annex C.2.

question: An ATS Section 9 thermographic report must state:
choices: The emissivity setting used for every image
The load conditions at the time
The imager's serial number and lens
The ambient humidity
explanation: The report lists the equipment, discrepancies, the temperature difference, the probable cause, areas inspected (including inaccessible ones), load conditions, photos and thermograms, and recommended action. Without load conditions, a delta-T means little. Source: ANSI/NETA ATS-2025 Section 9.

question: What minimum sensitivity does ATS Section 9 require of an infrared imager used for a survey?
choices: Able to detect a 1 °C difference at 30 °C
Able to detect a 0.1 °C difference at 100 °C
Able to detect a 5 °C difference at 20 °C
Any imager with a radiometric output
explanation: ATS asks for an imager that can resolve 1 °C of difference when the target is at 30 °C. ECS-2024 Section 9 sets the same figure. Source: ANSI/NETA ATS-2025 Section 9; ANSI/NETA ECS-2024 9.3.

question: A 100 A breaker terminal has a rated total temperature of 95 °C at a 40 °C rated ambient. It carries 50 A in 25 °C air and measures 45 °C. Using Gill's standards-based method with n = 2, the result is:
choices: Limit about 38.8 °C, so it is over spec
Corrected limit 95 °C, so the terminal is fine
Corrected limit about 52.5 °C, so the terminal is fine
Corrected limit about 65 °C, so it needs monitoring only
explanation: Ttc = (Trt - Tra) x (Im/Ir)^n + Tma = (95 - 40) x (0.5)^2 + 25 = 13.75 + 25 = 38.75 °C. The measured 45 °C exceeds that. Using n = 1 instead gives the wrong 52.5 °C. Source: Gill, Electrical Power Equipment Maintenance and Testing, 2nd ed., 8.10.2.2; ANSI/NETA ATS-2025 Table 100.18 note 2.
reference: Gill, Electrical Power Equipment Maintenance and Testing, 2nd ed., 8.10.2.2; ANSI/NETA ATS-2025 Table 100.18 note 2

question: A lug runs 6 °C above an identical lug on the next phase while the feeder is at 50% load. If heating goes with current squared, what delta-T would you expect at full load, and how does Table 100.18 rate it?
choices: About 12 °C, repair as time permits
About 6 °C, a possible deficiency
About 24 °C, a major discrepancy
About 9 °C, repair as time permits
explanation: Twice the current means four times the heating: 6 x 4 = 24 °C. Between similar components, over 15 °C is a major discrepancy. That is why load conditions must be in the report. Source: ANSI/NETA ATS-2025 Table 100.18 and note 1.

question: A heavily corroded connection shows a high emissivity and a modest temperature rise. Why can this still be misleading?
choices: Corroded surfaces always read 50 °C too hot
High emissivity means the camera sees only reflections
The rise depends on load; light load can hide it
Corrosion makes the surface transparent to infrared
explanation: Dull or corroded surfaces emit well, so the temperature reading is trustworthy. The rise itself depends on current. Gill notes heavier loading is better for finding problems, and ATS requires load conditions in the report. Source: Gill, Electrical Power Equipment Maintenance and Testing, 2nd ed., 8.10.2; IEEE C57.152-2025, Annex C.2; ANSI/NETA ATS-2025 Section 9.
reference: Gill, Electrical Power Equipment Maintenance and Testing, 2nd ed., 8.10.2; IEEE C57.152-2025, Annex C.2; ANSI/NETA ATS-2025 Section 9

question: A new lineup passed its acceptance infrared survey. Which follow-up do ATS and ECS offer as an optional test?
choices: A second survey within 12 months of acceptance
A repeat survey every week for the first month
A survey at no load within 30 days
No follow-up; acceptance surveys are final
explanation: Both ATS Section 9 and ECS 9.1 list an optional follow-up survey within 12 months of final acceptance, once the system has run under real loading. Source: ANSI/NETA ATS-2025 Section 9; ANSI/NETA ECS-2024 9.1.2.
